items.title: Harrison Barnes Interview, 1959-01-29
items.q: I've heard him when I used to be in the park... You see, you take like Manuel Perez, well, he was more of a music man. He had a pretty good band.

ctx.x: Do you remember a carnet player, Buddy Bolden? Did he ever get down there on excursion or anything?

Not that I know of. Bolden was on his way out when I got here. I heard him several times. He used to go around by the... He used to have a square right where the auditorium is now. That square that used to go straight across, used to be named Congo Square, the changes to Burgard Square. And they had a hall that's called the Globe Hall right there. Where you could sit down out in the square, when they're going to have a dance there, they'll come outside and play two, three numbers. That's where I heard Bolden,…
Did you hear Bolden after you moved up here or did you come up here on a visit sometime before...

items.title: Harrison Barnes Interview, 1959-01-29
items.q: old man Martinez, he took the band over after he got a... So they asked me to play one day... So I had been playing... And we played with them

ctx.x: And they got a, my dad didn't know what he was doing.

He was going to be a little bit of a little bit of a little bit of a little bit of a little of a little bit of a little bit of a little bit of a band. And then they got a, my dad's man, by the name of old man Martinez, he took the band over after he got a, and Gilbert, before he left, he bought a whole lot of orchestration. You know, you want to set up band with that. So they had the same Sonny Henry playing the trombone. And they practiced and practiced and practiced. So they asked me to play one day. I don't…
What's the name, but the name's not again?
